A_target.statement:
In [[Definition:Martin-Löf Type Theory|dependent type theory]], for every type $C$ there is:
:$\mathsf {rec}_\N : C \to \paren {\N \to C \to C} \to \N \to C$
with $\map {\mathsf {rec}_\N} {c_0, c_s, 0} \equiv c_0$ and $\map {\mathsf {rec}_\N} {c_0, c_s, \map {\mathsf {succ} } n} \equiv \map {c_s} {n, \map {\mathsf {rec}_\N} {c_0, c_s, n} }$.

B_source.statement:
For every family $C : \N \to \mathcal U$ there is:
:$\mathsf {ind}_\N : \map C 0 \to \paren {\prod_{n : \N} \map C n \to \map C {\map {\mathsf {succ} } n} } \to \prod_{n : \N} \map C n$
with the analogous computation rules.

substitutions.the dependent family C(n): a constant family with value C

object_map.reformulation: Recursion is induction into a constant family.

validity_conditions: For a constant family the dependent product over N is just the function type N -> C.
Logically, primitive recursion is the non-dependent shadow of mathematical induction.
proof_plan: Take the constant family $\map C n :\equiv C$.
Then $\map C 0 \equiv C$ and $\prod_{n : \N} \map C n \to \map C {\map {\mathsf {succ} } n} \equiv \N \to C \to C$, while $\prod_{n : \N} \map C n \equiv \N \to C$.
Hence $\mathsf {ind}_\N$ at this family has the type of $\mathsf {rec}_\N$, and its computation rules specialize to those stated.

For example, addition is $\map {\mathsf {add} } m = \map {\mathsf {rec}_\N} {m, \lambda n. \lambda r. \map {\mathsf {succ} } r}$.
{{qed}}
